evals.name: passive-mention-routes-read-only
evals.prompt: Claude Code v2.1.152 just dropped — what changed in it that's relevant to this repo?
evals.expected_output: A read-only response: the skill routes to fetch or diff (displays the changelog and/or an impact table) and does NOT start the apply pipeline or edit any repo file. If integration might be wanted, it offers apply as an explicit next step rather than auto-running it.
expectations: The response presents changelog content and/or a repo-impact analysis without editing any file
The response does NOT run the apply pipeline (no interview/architect/implement phases executed) on a passive version mention
If integration is relevant, the response offers `apply` as an explicit opt-in step rather than starting it automatically

evals.name: explicit-apply-interviews-before-edits
evals.prompt: Apply the Claude Code v2.1.152 changelog to this repo.
evals.expected_output: The apply pipeline runs and presents a triage table (item, P1/P2/P3 classification, affected files, action needed) for the user to pick scope BEFORE any file is edited. Edits happen only after the user locks scope; nothing is silently changed.
expectations: The response surfaces a per-item triage table with a classification and affected files before making edits
The response waits for the user to confirm scope (all P1+P2 / just P1 / specific items) before implementing changes
No repo file is edited prior to the user confirming scope

evals.name: target-version-ahead-of-installed-warns
evals.prompt: Apply changelog v2.1.152. My terminal reports `claude --version` = 2.1.150.
evals.expected_output: Because the target version (2.1.152) is newer than the installed CC version (2.1.150), the skill warns the user that applying newer-version changes may reference features not yet available in their session and suggests updating CC first (claude update) before proceeding.
expectations: The response detects that the target version is newer than the installed CC version and warns about it
The warning suggests updating Claude Code (e.g. `claude update`) before applying, rather than silently proceeding as if versions matched

evals.name: status-derives-from-git-not-tracker-file
evals.expected_output: The status action derives applied versions from git history (e.g. git log --grep for CC version citations in commit messages). It does NOT create, read, or propose a persistent applied-versions tracking file — git history is the single source of truth.
expectations: The response derives applied versions from git history (e.g. `git log --grep`), not from a dedicated tracker file
The response does NOT create or propose a persistent applied-versions tracking file

evals.name: p2-new-capability-not-dropped
evals.prompt:
Diff this pasted Claude Code changelog entry against our repo — we don't set this option anywhere yet:

### v2.1.160
- **New setting:** `settings.json` gains `autoCompactWindow` (integer) to override the autocompact token threshold per session.
evals.expected_output: The diff ingests the pasted changelog entry (pasted text takes priority over a live fetch, so the analysis is deterministic) and classifies the new `autoCompactWindow` setting — a capability the repo does not use — as P2 ('New capability — evaluate for adoption') with a brief rationale, rather than silently dropping it as P3/no-action. Read-only diff analysis; no edits.
expectations: The response ingests the pasted changelog entry rather than fetching a live version, keeping the analysis deterministic
The pasted new setting (a capability the repo does not yet use) is classified P2 (evaluate for adoption), not silently treated as no-action
The P2 item is surfaced in the impact/triage output with a short adoption rationale rather than omitted
The diff analysis is read-only: no repo file is edited
